title: LLM Model Fallback: a second model answers
lede: An LLM key can name a second model to answer with when its first is down, overloaded or out of budget, including a different provider; the fallback carries its own budget so the agent keeps serving within a known ceiling (release notes). The order of attempts, the answer naming the serving model and the refusal are the lab’s own model.

sub: Calls the gateway with its LLM key

sub: The key names a second model for when its first cannot answer

steps.title: The app calls with its key
steps.what: The request reaches the gateway with the LLM key. The key names a second model to answer with if its first cannot.

steps.title: First model first
steps.what: In the lab model the gateway tries the key’s first model first.

steps.title: Healthy first model answers
steps.what: When the first model is healthy it answers and no fallback is attempted (lab model). The answer goes back to the app.
steps.why: Lab model: the trace shows one attempt and names the model that served.

steps.title: First model cannot answer
steps.what: If the first model is down, overloaded or out of budget, the key’s second model answers instead.
steps.why: From the release notes: down, overloaded or out of budget. UNVERIFIED: what counts as overloaded, whether a retry comes first, what happens mid-stream, and whether AI Guard runs again on the fallback’s answer.

steps.title: Fallback answers
steps.what: The fallback model answers. It can be a different provider and carries its own budget, so the agent keeps serving within a known ceiling. Charging its spend to its own budget and not the first model’s is the lab model.
steps.why: How the answer names the serving model is lab model and UNVERIFIED.

steps.title: Both budgets exhausted
steps.what: In the lab model, when the fallback’s budget is spent as well, the call is refused with a named refusal that says which budgets ran out, never a blank page.
steps.why: Lab model: the refusal wording and shape are the lab’s own and UNVERIFIED against the product.
